headline: An AI-infrastructure selloff swamped the market while defensives and energy held up
push: Tech and AI names sank while staples, energy and health care held up.
summary: The S&P 500 (SPY) finished the week -1.97%, but the damage was lopsided. The Nasdaq 100 (QQQ) was -5.52% and small caps (IWM) -3.05%, while the Dow 30 (DIA) was +0.58% and the S&P 500 equal-weight (RSP) +0.49%. Information Technology (XLK) -7.70% was by far the weakest sector, and Consumer Staples (XLP) +5.02%, Energy (XLE) +4.86% and Health Care (XLV) +3.45% led. AI-linked names bore the brunt, with CoreWeave (CRWV) -25.21%, Nebius (NBIS) -25.15% and Dell Technologies (DELL) -22.92% for the week. The VIX closed Friday at 19.99, up from 14.84 a week earlier. Oil kept climbing: the WTI fund (USO) was +9.15% for the week. Seven of the 11 sectors rose, and 171 of the 275 names the dashboard tracks finished higher.
mood_detail: The VIX rose from 14.84 to 19.99 (+34.70%), the biggest jump in weeks, and the Nasdaq 100 (QQQ) -5.52% sharply lagged the equal-weight S&P 500 (RSP) +0.49%. Most stocks held up; the pain sat in AI and tech.

headlines: Columbus Day session: the Dow rose to about 51,850 while the S&P 500 (SPY) was -0.06% and the Nasdaq slipped; defensive sectors led while semiconductors and optical networking lagged.
Ciena (CIEN) -9.99% and Lumentum (LITE) -9.78% were among the biggest decliners.
Indexes finished nearly flat: the S&P 500 closed at 7,805.45 and the Nasdaq at 27,204.38.
Energy led: Energy (XLE) +3.26% as WTI crude (CL) rose to $94.99 (+1.33%).
Applied Materials (AMAT) -6.69%, Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) -5.70% and Citigroup (C) -5.60% were among the biggest decliners.
Tech sold off: S&P 500 (SPY) -1.08%, the VIX rose to 16.87 and Information Technology (XLK) -2.98% while Health Care (XLV) +2.53%.
CoreWeave (CRWV) -15.46% and Dell Technologies (DELL) -11.36% led the decliners after a Barclays downgrade of AI server makers.
UnitedHealth (UNH) +4.76% led the names the dashboard tracks.
A partial rebound: S&P 500 (SPY) +0.28%, with 185 of 276 tracked names rising.
Software led the bounce: AppLovin (APP) +6.52%, Intuit (INTU) +6.36% and ServiceNow (NOW) +6.15%.
Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) -7.10% and Dell Technologies (DELL) -6.67% kept falling.
The week ended with a rout in AI infrastructure: S&P 500 (SPY) -1.11% and the VIX closed at 19.98.
Nebius (NBIS) -12.18% and CoreWeave (CRWV) -11.91% fell as concern grew over AI debt; Strategy (MSTR) -9.56%.
Energy names such as Targa Resources (TRGP) +4.31% and Diamondback Energy (FANG) +4.27% rose.

sources.name: Investing Live: AI names fall as Nasdaq comes under pressure

themes.title: AI infrastructure under pressure
themes.text: CoreWeave (CRWV) -25.21%, Nebius (NBIS) -25.15%, Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) -24.95% and Dell Technologies (DELL) -22.92% led the week's decliners. Reports tied the selling to a Barclays downgrade of AI server makers and widening spreads on AI-related high-yield debt.

themes.title: Defense and energy held up
themes.text: Consumer Staples (XLP) +5.02%, Energy (XLE) +4.86% and Health Care (XLV) +3.45% led the 11 sectors. Seven rose and four fell: Information Technology (XLK) -7.70%, Industrials (XLI) -0.88%, Consumer Discretionary (XLY) -0.35% and Communication Services (XLC) -0.05%.

themes.title: Oil and bonds
themes.text: The WTI fund (USO) was +9.15% for the week and 20+ year Treasuries (TLT) +2.65%, so yields fell as investors sought safety. The 10-year yield ended the week near 5.09%, down from 5.24% on Monday.

themes.title: Fear picked up
themes.text: The VIX closed at 19.99, up from 14.84 a week earlier, as the tech selloff deepened on Friday.

questions: Information Technology (XLK) -7.70% while the equal-weight S&P 500 (RSP) was +0.49%: is this a contained AI unwind, or the start of something broader?
Falling yields and rising oil sent mixed signals. Which one is the market trusting more?
